beta.notes:
Native Plex client for MiSTer. Built for CRTs at 480i over Component, RGB, S-Video or Composite, with 480p on HDMI.

Beta access. This is a paid early-access build. Install and browsing work without a code. Playback needs the code from the MisterZine Patreon post. Stable releases will be free and codeless.

New in beta.15
- Continue Watching is back for servers with a very long playlist. A playlist longer than about 25 days (a big music playlist, say) made Home skip the whole Continue Watching row and start with the first library.
- Cleaner RGB picture. In 480i and 240p the first 12 and last 8 pixels of each line are now always black. Some RGB chains (transcoders, receivers, some TVs) take a line's black level from its first pixels, and a picture that started there showed dark or green lines that moved with the picture. These pixels sit in the CRT's overscan. 480p keeps every pixel.
- Video geometry shows where those black line ends are ("12 pixels in (minimum)"), and a saved picture area now changes only at the edges you move.
- Better reports after an update. When an update restarts Plex, the launch is logged, and a failed FFmpeg download says why it failed.
- Playback keeps the picture alive from a thread at the player's priority, and logs any late renewal to help track down brief black cuts. If the picture goes black while the sound plays on, please use Options > Send a report before quitting.

Everything from beta.14 is included.

Requirements
- Networked MiSTer on current MiSTer Linux
- 250 MB free on the SD card
- Plex account with a server that can transcode

Install
1. Download the Beta installer below and put it in the SD card's Scripts folder.
2. Run it from Scripts.
3. Follow the sign-in screen at plex.tv/link.

Already on an earlier beta: open Options > Updates in the app and install from there.

NTSC 480i only; PAL isn't supported yet.

This is unstable beta software. It talks to your real Plex account: playback, watched marks and resume points change your library, and a bug could change them wrongly. Use it at your own risk; no responsibility is taken for what it does to your library or your MiSTer.
